A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoCapAnything and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary material. The complete 13-page v1 and 14-page v2 support comparison, including matching material relocated into the appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original GenZoo comparisons, modality and architecture ablations in Tables 1–3, and qualitative motion-capture and retargeting results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, revised ablation results, IK animation examples, and an average rotation error.

M1.justification: The reference encoder, visual and geometry streams, motion decoder, position-only training loss, and two-stage IK procedure remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of mesh conditioning, reference selection, and sliding-window inference do not establish changes to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Coverage remains Truebones Zoo, Objaverse humanoid assets, wild-animal videos, and cross-species retargeting. V2's taxonomy counts describe the existing 60-sequence benchmark. The new multi-view IK displays are output visualizations, not new input-camera scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds evaluated HRNet, ViTPose, VIBE, and GLoT baselines across seen, rare, and unseen species. GenZoo remains: its original quantitative comparison moves from v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 4, with its qualitative comparison moved to Figure 8.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a substantial additional comparison protocol: four adapted baselines are retrained on the same training set with unified skeleton representations and input modalities, topology-matched outputs, and MPJPE/MPJVE evaluation across three splits. It also reports geodesic rotation evaluation after IK. Existing splits and training budgets remain unchanged; newly disclosed mesh and scaling settings do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds multi-view IK-driven animation case studies in Section 4.8 and Figure 3, extending the earlier appendix's brief IK visualization discussion. Section 8 also reports a brief observation about substituting predicted meshes for ground-truth meshes. The modality-removal and layer-depth ablation designs are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. V2's additional averages remain point estimates rather than new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 contain revised scores: full-model seen/rare/unseen MPJPE changes from 8.06/12.04/25.63 to 1.06/1.28/1.76. V2 also adds four-baseline results and approximately 17 degrees average geodesic rotation error. These are revised or newly reported results, not established same-setting performance gains, given v1's unspecified evaluation scaling and mesh conditioning. The relocated GenZoo CD-Skeleton values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation, attention equation, position loss, IK derivations and regularizers, and CD-Skeleton definition are retained. Their relocation and renumbering introduce no new assumptions, mathematical reasoning, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing CAMoCap, proposing the factorized MoCapAnything framework, curating Truebones Zoo, and supporting generalization and cross-species retargeting. Additional experiments strengthen support without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds rationales for scale normalization and ground-truth-mesh evaluation, explains GenZoo's incompatibility with joint-aligned metrics, and frames the selected network depth as a capacity-versus-complexity tradeoff. The existing limitations concerning reconstruction quality, known rigs, camera-space operation, and absent physics/contact reasoning remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents evaluation units and ground-truth mesh conditioning, benchmark taxonomy counts, same-species reference selection, paired supervision, long-video inference, and an example mesh predictor, SWIFT4D. Reported hardware changes from eight 32-GB NPUs to eight 64-GB GPUs. The abstract now explicitly declares code available through the project page; availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to PoseAug, PoseTriplet, and GLoT. The relocated GenZoo discussion changes its positioning from the only existing applicable state-of-the-art method to among the few relevant works. The broader positioning against fixed-template pose and motion-capture approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are concentrated in the experimental and supplementary sections: rewritten baseline and ablation passages, a new IK subsection, relocated GenZoo discussion, and expanded implementation prose. An affiliation is also updated. Most introductory, methodological, and concluding language remains stable.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially reorganized: v2 adds baseline Table 1 and a large multi-view IK Figure 3, revises Figures 2 and 4, and compresses and relocates ablation Tables 2–3 into one column. The original GenZoo figure and table move into the supplement as Figure 8 and Table 4.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through additional controlled baseline comparisons and the first numerical IK assessment, while clarifying evaluation units and reliance on ground-truth geometry. These improve support and transparency. The gains remain qualified by unreconciled ablation-score revisions, sparse adaptation and rotation-evaluation details, and the absence of quantified evidence for the claimed negligible degradation with predicted meshes.
